channel.title: Twinthos Notes
channel.description: Original investigations and sourced analysis about intelligent systems and the work they change. Six desks: Business, Models, Futures, The Lab, Agents, The Brief.

item.title: Five of the world's largest software companies shipped company memory in eight days. Most businesses still do not have one.
item.description: Dell, SAP, Google, Meta and Workday all shipped something that remembers what a business knows. Meanwhile staff spend 2.3 hours a week re-typing context an AI should already have — about GBP 29,900 a year for a ten-person firm, on something that produces no output at all.

item.title: Half of small businesses already let AI do a person’s job. Their teams are exhausted.
item.description: A survey of 729 owners found 53% say AI now absorbs a full-time role — and 65% say running a leaner team has hurt their wellbeing. This is not a story about robots taking jobs. It is a story about people being used as middleware.

item.title: The AI that answers your phone now costs $2 a month. Almost nobody has switched.
item.description: On 14 October 2026 Google shipped its long-running agent model at $2 per million input tokens. A week earlier OpenAI started rolling out always-on agents. The economics of a digital employee have collapsed — but the reasons businesses have not moved have nothing to do with price.

item.title: 95% of AI pilots fail. The number has been stable for two years.
item.description: MIT’s August 2025 State of AI in Business report found roughly 95% of generative AI pilots produced no measurable P&L impact. McKinsey and BCG independently report the same wall. The pattern behind it is not technical — and it is fixable.

item.title: A digital employee costs £1.60 an hour. The junior it replaces costs £13.
item.description: The maths of replacing a human role with software, done honestly with October 2026 list pricing: the model costs almost nothing, the true cost of running it properly is the interesting part, and the number that changes minds is the staff-hour, not the invoice.

item.title: The last time a machine was supposed to erase a job. It hired more people instead.
item.description: Everyone knows ATMs replaced bank tellers. The data says the opposite: teller employment rose for two decades after the ATMs arrived, because the machine cut the cost of a branch and banks opened more of them. There is a live lesson for anyone reading this week’s AI headlines.

item.title: Everyone is shipping an “AI agent” this month. Almost none of them are agents.
item.description: Google, OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic all released something called an agent in October 2026. The word now covers everything from a chatbot to a worker with its own computer. Here is what actually separates the two — and why it decides whether your business gets a colleague or a demo.
